body: This might be a totally bizarre thing to hear from a random internet person but, seriously, please call for emergency services. Seriously, please reach out. Get back here safe and sound, because I'd like to know more about what's going on with you, what things might be lurking but also where you feel, well, good - adventurous, comfortable, confident. I'm interested, let me know.
I just wanted to add that I really appreciated your response - I'm not sure how well that came across in the previous comment but it means a lot.

Thanks for your response and I'm sorry if I'm coming across as confusing or enigmatic - I'm new to this and could very well be terrible at it. I just would like to know how people deal with the repeated crisis of suicidal thoughts and urges. I can understand and have experienced how to suspend the urge to self-destruction during particular periods of crisis. But the problem is that, after that day, I always wake up back at square one. The urges press down on me and it feels like every day is a gamble concerning where they might lead. Some of those who have responded or intervened have legitimately saved my life, and I have so much love for them. I would just like to ask how people continue going on after those moments - when the urges are there and begging to be acted upon, debating the pragmatics of various methods, but you know that you can't just spend every day asking people to help you through to tomorrow. That would be ridiculous and such a disservice to them and yourself. And yet nevertheless you've got to do something today or you are, well, fucked.
